facts.text: It is olive-brown above and buff below, with a brown head, nape and throat.
facts.quote: it is olive-brown above and buff below, with a brown head, nape and throat

facts.text: A patch of bare skin over its eye is cream or orange, and its legs and feet are orange.
facts.quote: a cream or orange patch of bare skin over the eye, and a dull white crescent-shaped patch on the nape. The legs and feet are orange.

facts.text: It makes a scratchy chwik-chwik-chwik call.
facts.quote: It makes a scratchy chwik-chwik-chwik call.

facts.text: Insects form the bulk of the brown-headed honeyeater's diet.
facts.quote: Insects form the bulk of the diet

facts.text: It forages by probing in the bark of trunks and branches of trees.
facts.quote: the brown-headed honeyeater forages by probing in the bark of trunks and branches of trees.

facts.text: Brown-headed honeyeaters may nest from July to December, breeding once or twice during this time.
facts.quote: Brown-headed honeyeaters may nest from July to December, breeding once or twice during this time.

facts.text: The nest is a thick-walled bowl of grasses and bits of bark, hidden in the outer foliage of a tall tree, usually a eucalypt.
facts.quote: The nest is a thick-walled bowl of grasses and bits of bark, lined with softer plant material, hidden in the outer foliage of a tall tree, usually a eucalypt.

facts.text: Two or three shiny, buff-pink eggs sparsely spotted with red-brown are laid.
facts.quote: Two or three eggs are laid, 16 x 13 mm in size, and shiny, buff-pink, sparsely spotted with red-brown

facts.text: It is endemic to Australia and lives in temperate forests and Mediterranean-type shrubby vegetation.
facts.quote: It is endemic to Australia. Its natural habitats are temperate forests and Mediterranean-type shrubby vegetation.
